# INTRX — The Interaction Library

> A curated, copy-paste library of the web interactions used by award-winning
> design agencies. 399 native patterns are implemented, including the full 52-entry DRAMS collection.
> Each pattern ships three things: a live demo, a single-file HTML+CSS+JS
> snippet, and an LLM prompt that specifies the interaction precisely enough
> to rebuild it in any framework.

Site: https://intrx.vercel.app
Registry: https://intrx.vercel.app/registry/index.json
License: MIT; photographs under the Unsplash License with per-component attribution. DRAMS by 1042 Studio (@mrblackstudio and @karimeshrimp).

## Buttons & Micro

### Border Beam (`btn-border-beam`)

Build an original self-contained Border Beam control matching the v4 INTRX tile: one 160 by 40px charcoal Deploy button, 12px corners, a 1px white border at 11% opacity, a white 16px lightning icon and 13.5px medium Inter. Center it on a transparent 260 by 100 design plane. The shell supplies the stage and dock; render no outer panel, header, measurement labels or replay/reset buttons. Use the supplied local SVG icon, 121 by 1px perimeter highlight and 76 by 32px glow without resizing their intrinsic dimensions. A regular rounded-rectangle CSS motion path moves the light around the button over 2000ms linear. Pause/resume retains its current position, and a shell replay action returns to the top-center peak frame. Press scales to .97 over 80ms ease-out; release takes 250ms ease-pop. Expose toggle and replay through ctx.onAction and announce button activation through a live status and ctx.emit. Under reduced motion freeze the top-center highlight, keep keyboard focus and activation feedback, and use a 150ms opacity press response. Support native Enter/Space, runtime suspension, declared geometry and portable local assets.

Center it on a transparent 260 by 100 design plane. Render no specimen card, telemetry labels or internal toolbar. A masked neutral gradient with a 26px soft white band and background-size 400% sweeps from background-position 100% to 0% over 2000ms linear, repeating while visible. Expose toggle and replay with ctx.onAction; pause retains the exact position and replay restarts the pass. Use a native button with visible focus, Enter/Space activation, a live status and ctx.emit for the invitation action. Press to .97 in 80ms ease-out and release in 250ms ease-pop. Keep running/sweeps/entries/inside/activations telemetry off the visible surface. Reduced motion renders the centered still sheen and uses 150ms opacity feedback. The shell owns the stage, lifecycle, fit and dock controls.

### Jelly Press (`btn-jelly-press`)

Build an original tactile Jelly Press matching the v4 tile: a single soft #f1f1f1 button measuring 140 by 36px, 12px corners, a restrained shadow, dark #111 text and 13px medium Inter reading Press and hold. Center it on a transparent 260 by 100 design plane. Hold to compress to scale(1.10,.82) over 80ms ease-out around a 50% 65% origin and reduce the shadow. Keep the squash until the matching primary pointer or Space/Enter is released; do not run a timed one-shot while the user is holding. On release read the actual current transform and use a time-based spring with stiffness 380, damping 32 and mass 1, integrated in 1/120s steps, to return to rest with a small rebound. Preserve position if a fresh press interrupts the spring. Capture the pointer so an outside release is handled; cancellation, lost capture, blur and replay must release or clear safely. Ignore duplicate/secondary presses and key repeats while preserving native button activation. Expose run through ctx.onAction for a simulated 250ms hold, plus replay for immediate cancellation. Use wrapped timers and frames, remove window listeners on disposal, keep visible focus and a hidden live status, and emit native activations. Reduced motion keeps the shape static and provides a 150ms opacity change while held. No demo-owned panels or reset buttons; every class starts with d-jelly-demo.

## Navigation & Menus

### Fullscreen Menu (`menu-fullscreen-overlay`)

Use a native 300 by 320 composition. Replace manifesto text with a photographic four-face editorial navigation card. Use locally bundled Inter at weights 400–550 for UI and every numerical readout, with tabular numerals and normal tracking. Monospace is reserved for actual code or ASCII. Preserve pointer, keyboard, deterministic fixtures, reset behavior and lifecycle contracts. Build a self-contained CSS 3D cube navigation demo with four semantic content faces. Use perspective on the scene, preserve-3d on the cube, and four faces at 0, 90, 180, and -90 degrees with translateZ equal to half the cube width. The active face must snap to exact 90-degree rotations with a physical cubic-bezier transition.

Provide four visible navigation tabs plus keyboard controls: arrows move one face, Home selects the first, and End selects the last. Horizontal pointer dragging previews the rotation continuously; release snaps by distance to the nearest face, with a small committed-swipe threshold. Wheel input advances one face with a short lockout. Keep rotation turns unbounded internally so transitions take the shortest wrapped route.

Synchronize the active tab, counter, aria-current, aria-hidden face states, and a polite live status. Include pointer capture, touch-action pan-y, visible focus, responsive cube depth, reduced-motion handling, completely scoped CSS, and no dependencies.

Every card has front and back faces using backface-visibility hidden, a preserve-3d inner wrapper, and a 180-degree Y rotation. A card click flips only that card and keeps aria-pressed, its action label, a revealed counter, and live status synchronized.

Add a master Reveal all / Conceal all control. When activated, derive each transition delay from its grid row and column: revealing uses (row+column)*85ms so a wave travels top-left to bottom-right; concealing uses ((1-row)+(3-column))*85ms so it reverses from bottom-right. Clear delays after the last transition so later individual clicks respond immediately.

Include hover lift without losing the current flip angle, visible focus, responsive two-column presentation, reduced-motion handling that removes duration and stagger, fully scoped CSS, and no dependencies.

### WebGL Point Globe (`webgl-point-globe`)

Use a native 300 by 320 composition. Give the globe quiet negative space and remove coordinate crosshair clutter. Use locally bundled Inter at weights 400–550 for UI and every numerical readout, with tabular numerals and normal tracking. Monospace is reserved for actual code or ASCII. Preserve pointer, keyboard, deterministic fixtures, reset behavior and lifecycle contracts. Build a self-contained raw WebGL rotating point globe with exactly 1,800 vertices distributed on a unit sphere using the Fibonacci/golden-angle method: y=1-2*i/(count-1), radius=sqrt(1-y²), theta=π*(3-sqrt(5))*i. Upload one static vec3 buffer and draw GL_POINTS with additive alpha blending.

In the vertex shader rotate each point by yaw and pitch, project it with depth=3.15-z, and compute distance from projected clip position to a uPointer ray. Points within 0.32 clip units swell smoothly up to 4.5x and brighten; front-facing points are also larger/brighter. The fragment shader must discard outside a circular point and render a soft mint core.

Auto-rotate slowly, damp yaw/pitch by 8%, drag to orbit, pointer move updates the shader ray/reticle/lat-lon labels, click or Enter/Space pauses, arrows nudge yaw, and Reset restores orbit. Clamp DPR to 2, resize with ResizeObserver, pause offscreen, support reduced motion, expose WebGL/point-count data attributes for verification, provide visible focus, scoped CSS, and no dependencies.

### WebGL Wobbly Sphere (`webgl-wobbly-sphere`)

Build a self-contained raw WebGL wobbly sphere using an indexed UV mesh with 48 longitude segments and 32 latitude segments (1,617 vertices, 3,072 triangles). Upload static position and Uint16 index buffers and draw filled triangles with depth testing and back-face culling.

In the vertex shader, layer three sine waves over x/y/z, then add a higher-frequency impulse multiplied by uEnergy. Scale each vertex radially by 1 + wave*uAmplitude + impulse*0.14. Apply yaw/pitch tilt, perspective-project, and pass approximate radial normal/wave to a fragment shader with diffuse, grayscale rim, and a single orange accent shading.

Derive pointer energy from pixel distance divided by event time, clamp to 1, then decay target energy by 0.965 per 16ms and damp displayed energy by 16%. Pointer position controls target tilt. Calm/Fluid/Wild presets change amplitude and time speed; click or Enter/Space freezes; arrows inject energy. Clamp DPR to 2, resize, pause offscreen, respect reduced motion, expose renderer/mesh counts, provide focus/live state, scoped CSS, and no dependencies.

## Cursor

### Cursor Gooey Blob (`cursor-gooey-blob`)

Build a self-contained gooey cursor navigation interaction in a 320px position-relative root. Put one 54px circular pointer blob and three 80×44px pill-shaped navigation masses inside a single layer using an SVG filter. The filter must blur SourceGraphic by 10px, then apply a color matrix whose alpha row is 0 0 0 22 -9, and composite the crisp source atop the thresholded mass. Render the 11px mono button labels in a separate unfiltered three-column flexible nav layer so text stays sharp.

Track pointer coordinates relative to the root and constrain the blob center by its 27px radius. Animate with one requestAnimationFrame loop using a damped spring: velocity = (velocity + (target - position) * stiffness) * damping, then position += velocity. Use stiffness 0.095 and damping 0.76 while free; on button hover or keyboard focus, retarget to that button's local center with stiffness 0.16 and damping 0.68. While captured, ease the blob toward scaleX 2.45 and scaleY 0.96. While moving freely, add up to 0.42 horizontal stretch and subtract up to 0.18 vertical scale based on min(1, speed / 22), and rotate to atan2(vy, vx). Ease scale components by 0.16 per frame.

Use only transform for frame-by-frame DOM writes, cache queried nodes, and keep pointermove passive. Buttons must remain semantic, keyboard-focusable, and show a high-contrast focus ring. Announce hover/focus/selection state in a polite live region. For prefers-reduced-motion, stop interpolation and render the target position and scale immediately; keep the goo filter and keyboard behavior functional. The idle blob may use a subtle 2.8-second breathing animation, disabled for reduced motion.

Final typography: Use Inter for the main display or interface text. Use Inter for actions and readable interface copy; retain regular Inter counters, coordinates and technical annotations. Keep material borders subdued and gradients broad with continuous, gentle falloff.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders. Any deliberate Newsreader editorial text in the source remains editorial, not UI.

### Cursor Particle Emitter (`cursor-particle-emitter`)

Build a self-contained cursor particle emitter inside a 320px position-relative root. Use one full-size decorative canvas, a velocity readout, and a real keyboard-focusable “Launch burst” button. Resize the backing canvas to the root bounds, cap devicePixelRatio at 2, and set the drawing transform to DPR so all simulation coordinates remain in CSS pixels.

On pointermove, calculate local coordinates, distance from the previous sample, elapsed milliseconds clamped to at least 8, and velocity = min(1800, distance / elapsed * 1000). Emit one particle for roughly every 9px traveled, capped at 12 per event, interpolating spawn positions along the segment so fast pointer events do not create gaps. Give particles an initial impulse opposite the pointer direction with magnitude min(260, 28 + velocity * 0.12), plus up to ±35px/s lateral jitter. Slow movement creates 0.9–2.2px dust; velocity above 620px/s creates occasional 3.3px white sparks. On pointerdown or button activation, emit 34–48 particles around a full circle with randomized 0.45–1.1 energy multipliers.

Run one requestAnimationFrame loop. Clamp delta time to 32ms, apply exponential horizontal drag pow(0.985, dt * 60), vertical drag pow(0.992, dt * 60), and gravity of 520px/s². Each particle stores its previous position; draw a round line from that point opposite 0.018 times velocity, then a small circular head. Lifetimes range from 0.32–1.0 seconds and alpha equals remainingLife / maxLife. Cap the pool at 220 particles, remove dead or offstage particles in reverse order, cache DOM references, and keep pointer listeners passive.

The canvas must be aria-hidden; announce button and pointer bursts through a polite live region, retain an obvious focus ring, and keep touch input working with touch-action none. Under prefers-reduced-motion, clear the prior field on each interaction, emit at most 12 particles with zero velocity, skip gravity and lifetime decay, and render a representative static constellation instead of moving trails.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders. Any deliberate Newsreader editorial text in the source remains editorial, not UI.

### Cursor Elastic Line (`cursor-elastic-line`)

Convert pointer coordinates from the root bounding rectangle into viewBox coordinates. Clamp the target control point to x=110–690 and y=42–278. Simulate the rendered control point with a damped spring on each requestAnimationFrame: velocity = (velocity + (target - position) * 0.085) * 0.78, then position += velocity. On pointerleave, return the target to (400,160); retain velocity so the cable overshoots and rings down naturally. On pointerdown, add a 68px/s vertical impulse opposite the side of the baseline that was pressed to create a visible pluck.

Update both path d attributes and the node cx/cy once per frame. Calculate displayed tension as min(99, round(distance(control, baselineCenter) / 2.45)). Cache all elements and bounding-box reads outside the animation loop; use a single rAF and passive pointer listeners. Do not animate layout properties.

Make the root keyboard-focusable with a visible inset focus ring. Arrow keys move the target by 16 viewBox units, Shift+Arrow by 34, Home and a semantic reset button return it to center. Prevent default only for those handled keys, announce the interaction source in a polite live region, and update aria-valuetext only when tension changes by at least 20 points. Under prefers-reduced-motion, disable dash animation and spring interpolation, snapping the control point directly to the target while preserving pointer and keyboard control.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders. ### Cursor Grid Ripple (`cursor-grid-ripple`)

Build a self-contained canvas dot-grid ripple inside a 320px position-relative root. Create an evenly centered grid with 32px spacing on desktop and 28px on narrow stages, leaving roughly 32px outer margins. Each dot stores rest position, x/y displacement, and residual energy. Resize the backing canvas to the root, cap devicePixelRatio at 2, keep simulation coordinates in CSS pixels, and rebuild the grid only on resize.

Represent each wave as {x, y, radius, life, power}. Pointer movement emits when travel exceeds 34px or 80ms has elapsed; derive velocity from distance / max(8ms, elapsed), then power = min(1.2, 0.55 + velocity / 1000). Pointerdown, Space, and a semantic center-launch button emit stronger 1.4–1.65 waves. Cap active waves at 7. Each frame clamp dt to 32ms, expand radius by (210 + power * 90)px/s, and reduce life by 0.55/s.

For every dot and wave, calculate distance and a Gaussian ring band: exp(-((distance - radius) / thickness)²) * life * power, where thickness = 18 + power * 10. Add normalized radial displacement * band * 17 and take the maximum band as target brightness. Ease offsets toward target by 0.24 per frame. Preserve a trailing afterimage with energy = max(targetEnergy, energy * pow(0.91, dt * 60)). Draw base dots at 1.25px in #2e2e34; affected dots grow by energy * 3.1px and brighten toward #fa7319. Use one rAF loop, cache state, remove dead/offstage waves, and keep pointer listeners passive.

Provide a visible emitter reticle, 00–99 amplitude readout, focus ring, arrow-key positioning (22px, or 40px with Shift), Home centering, Space launch, and polite status announcements. Prevent default only for handled keys and keep the launch button semantic. Under prefers-reduced-motion, keep one static wave at radius 68, do not expand or decay it, and assign displacement/energy directly without temporal easing; new interactions replace the previous static wave.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders. Any deliberate Newsreader editorial text in the source remains editorial, not UI.

Write one combined transform and opacity per frame. Cache DOM references, read bounds only in pointer/focus/resize handlers, keep pointermove passive, and clear the preview on pointerleave.

On keyboard focus, reveal the same preview positioned beside the focused link using its bounding box; hide on blur. Preserve obvious focus styling, prevent demo links from navigating, and announce the active project through a polite live region. ### Magnetic Button (`magnetic-button`)

Build magnetic buttons with GSAP.

Requirements:
- On mousemove over the button, compute the cursor offset from the button center.
- Translate the button toward the cursor at ~0.4 of the offset, and the inner label at ~0.7 (parallax between shell and label).
- Use gsap.to with power3.out, duration ~0.4s, so movement is smoothed.
- On mouseleave, both animate back to 0,0 with elastic.out(1, 0.35) over ~0.9s for a springy snap-back.
- The label must be pointer-events: none so it never steals hover.
- Disable on touch devices.
- If GSAP is unavailable, describe a vanilla fallback using lerp in requestAnimationFrame.

Render two compact 120px circular graphite controls with 12px mono labels and orange focus/interaction details. Keep 24px padding and a 22px gap so both remain visible in a narrow preview.

Final typography: Use Inter for the main display or interface text. Use Inter for actions and readable interface copy; retain regular Inter counters, coordinates and technical annotations. Keep material borders subdued and gradients broad with continuous, gentle falloff.

Use the final composition: regular Inter for interface text and all numerical values with tabular-nums; keep labels in sentence case, normal tracking, and weights 400–500. Remove decorative engineering headers, preserve functional controls and accessible status. Keep the native 320px stage and a restrained palette with subtle borders. Any deliberate Newsreader editorial text in the source remains editorial, not UI.

### Spring Cursor Follower (`spring-cursor-follower`)
